question.worked_solution:
To compute the integral of a general exponential function, we just need to divide by the natural logarithm of the base of the exponential function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{8})}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Using the laws of logarithms, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{8}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡8 \\  & =0-\operatorname{ln}⁡8 \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡8.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can simplify our final answer as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{8})}+C=-\frac{{(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}+C\end{aligned}
$$
